items.title: Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry
items.raw_text: As companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. But, Rao emphasizes, “it’s not about replacing scientific judgment; it is about giving our scientists better tools.” Scientists, data scientists, and IT teams approach problems from different perspectives, prioritizing experimental validity, model performance, and platform security and scalability, respectively. By bringing these groups together in “fusion teams,” Lubrizol aligns them around shared objectives

items.title: The climate case for AI has not been made
items.raw_text: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action. But so far, industries around the world aren’t doing nearly enough to harness the technology to actually drive down the greenhouse-gas emissions heating up the planet, despite some very optimistic claims from AI companies. In 2024, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman declared that AI would unleash “astounding triumphs,” including “fixing the climate.” The year before, in a 2023 op-ed , the head of sustainability at Google and her coauthor wrote that AI could reduce global emissions 5% to 10% by 2030. Some academic researchers have examined these AI-related climate claims. A peer-reviewed study published last year, led by researchers at the London School of Economics’ Grantham Research Institute and the firm Systemiq, estimated that AI could help cut global emissions by the equivalent of 3.2 to 5.4 billion tons of carbon dioxide annually by 2035—roughly on par with the US’s annual energy-related emissions on the high end, even after subtracting AI’s own energy footprint. Those potential gains are mostly concentrated in three sectors: power, meat and dairy, and vehicles. items.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind
items.raw_text: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions. They're too good at describing the work The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb. It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop! It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me! I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high level, what the PR is for and whether it deserves more of my attention. I think I've found a low-effort way to do this that feels right. Hide most of it in a details/summary The HTML <details><summary> elements render as a collapsed heading (the summary) that can be expanded to view the larger piece

items.title: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust
items.raw_text: Research: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust I was out walking the dog when I got curious about how easy/difficult it would be to write a SQLite C extension that adds a parse_number() function for turning strings like -$1,234.56 or '12.5%' into numeric values that could be summed and sorted. I fired up regular Claude chat (Opus 5.5) and prompted : I'm thinking about a SQLite custom function 'parse_number(value)' that strips ',', '$', '£' and '%', handles a leading '-', and returns 'NULL' for anything it can’t parse Explore the difference between building this as a SQLite extension in C v.s. in Rust - I want to compare performance and code complexity and size of the resulting .so (or whatever) file This gave me a solid starting point - the Rust extension was 321 KB (using Rusqlite ) and 298 KB (using sqlite-loadable-rs ), while the C extension was 14 KB. But the Rust extension was faster! Turns out that's because the Rust equivalent of C's strtod is "twice as fast". items.title: New Journal Article: Large Language Model Developments
items.raw_text: The full text article linked below was recently published by Royal Society Open Science. Title Large Language Model Developments Authors Philip Treleaven University College London Edward Sharkey University College London Sara Craciun University College London Source Royal Society Open Science (2026) 13 (11): 252099 DOI: 10.1098/rsos.252099 Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are generative artificial intelligence (AI) models trained with vast amounts of data and context, and excel at processing, understanding and generating human language, using transformer models to learn statistical relationships between tokens. LLMs are a subset of transformer models, and hence are closely related but not interchangeable. Given the ‘explosion’ of LLM research, the challenge is tracking emerging developments and matching LLMs to applications. This paper reviews LLM developments with the aim of understanding the underlying models’ computational strengths and weaknesses, building on previous work focusing on LLM optimization (Sharkey & Treleaven 2025 Optimising large language models: taxonomy and techniques. SSRN Scholarly Paper no. 5278456 . Rochester, NY: SSRN). We find that despite their power, LLMs (transformers) face several key challenges. items.title: Terry Pratchett's Study
items.raw_text: My comment on Terry Pratchett's Study — Hacker News. Terry Pratchett once wrote about the concept of "horizontal wealth". Vertical wealth is where you spend money on rich people stuff - yachts and suchlike. Horizontal wealth is where you spend more money on the things you liked before you got rich: https://chibuikeani.blogspot.com/2017/02/the-price-of-happin... But horizontal wealth means not letting your increased income dictate your tastes. You like books and now you have money? Buy more books! Change those catenary bookshelves for good hardwood ones! In my case, build a library extension to your office. And, of course, you buy what will be useful for that most wonderful of pursuits, blind research, which is research without direction for the sheer joy of it. (Original source is his book A Slip of the Keyboard - this linked blog post quotes that bit.) Tags: hacker-news , terry-pratchett

items.title: 🌐 🏢 IFLA MENA RDC & Bibliotheca Alexandrina Conclude Landmark Workshop on AI in Libraries 🤖 📚 ✨
items.raw_text: End of AI Workshop Group Photo The “Artificial Intelligence in Libraries” workshop, jointly organized by the IFLA Middle East and North Africa ( MENA ) Regional Division Committee and the Bibliotheca Alexandrina , has successfully concluded at the Library’s Multipurpose Hall on October 29 th 2026. The event brought together library professionals to address the growing role of emerging technologies in the field. Working in collaborative groups, participants drafted a preliminary practical framework for AI integration in libraries. The draft draws upon the Egyptian Supreme Council of Universities’ AI guide as well as international best practices and standards. In the coming weeks, participants will continue refining the document, with a strong focus on establishing a robust ethical framework for adoption of AI. To build on this momentum, the Bibliotheca Alexandrina and IFLA MENA will host follow-up events and training sessions over the coming months to expand the reach of the initiative and keep professionals abreast of key industry developments.

items.raw_text: Two of the top lawmakers backing the Pentagon's Golden Dome missile defense shield are among the wave of Republicans leaving Congress in the coming Democratic takeover, raising questions about the future of President Donald Trump's signature second-term defense initiative. The shakeup on Capitol Hill comes after military officials signaled in recent months that they might backpedal from one element Trump asked for in Golden Dome: the capability to shoot down missiles in their initial boost phase shortly after launch. The Golden Dome has escaped serious congressional scrutiny since Trump announced the program in January 2025, one week into his second term in the White House. That lack of scrutiny will change as Democrats take responsibility for writing the Pentagon's budget, introduce limits on funding, and put forth bills to strip out Golden Dome's most controversial component and give the program a new name. items.raw_text: Met Breaking Barriers wil de startup zijn marktaanpak aanscherpen en het aantal klanten verdrievoudigen. Het inzetten van AI voor klantcontact is voor bedrijven niet makkelijk. Klanten raken geïrriteerd van chatbots die niet goed werken en medewerkers hebben moeite met adoptie van alweer een nieuw systeem. Voor de startup DataSpeak genoeg reden om het anders aan te pakken. Zij hebben een platform ontwikkeld met AI-assistenten die klanten te woord staan via chat, telefoon, avatar, WhatsApp en e-mail, en dat aansluit op de systemen waarin medewerkers al werken. We spraken met mede-oprichter Arno van den Berg over AI in klantcontact en de groeidoelen van DataSpeak binnen Breaking Barriers. Zwitsers zakmes Arno werkte jarenlang in verschillende managementrollen bij techbedrijven. DataSpeak is zijn eerste eigen onderneming en voor het eerst zit hij aan de leverancierskant. Hij merkt dat zijn klanten worstelen met de toepasbare waarde van AI. Daarom begint DataSpeak met één toepassing en laat het eerst zien wat werkt, voordat het stap voor stap meer integraties toevoegt. Het platform van DataSpeak is dan ook modulair. Arno maakt de vergelijking met een Zwitsers zakmes. Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
items.raw_text: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. items.title: Kort: Nieuwe ict-crisis Amsterdam, Europese protesten tegen datacenters (en meer)
items.raw_text: In dit nieuwsoverzicht: vernieuwing erfpachtsysteem Amsterdam vertraagd, Schuberg Philis pikt DetACT-divisie op bij DataExpert, nieuwe inspecteur-generaal RDI, ai schrijft mee bij consulten in Maasstad Ziekenhuis en protesten tegen datacenters nemen toe. Opnieuw ict-problemen bij erfpachtsysteem gemeente Amsterdam De gemeente Amsterdam kampt opnieuw met problemen rond een belangrijk erfpachtsysteem. Zowel het bestaande systeem Hermes als diens beoogde opvolger Nise zorgt voor hoofdbrekens. Het nieuwe systeem had dit jaar in gebruik moeten worden genomen, maar de invoering is opnieuw vertraagd, meldt omroep AT5 . Tegelijkertijd is sinds oktober een groot deel van de technische ondersteuning voor het oude systeem weggevallen. Daardoor wordt het lastiger om storingen tijdig te verhelpen. Het systeem wordt gebruikt voor het beheer van erfpachtrechten en het berekenen en innen van erfpachtcanon. Volgens wethouder Alexander Scholtes waren de risico’s binnen de ambtelijke organisatie al maanden bekend. Een extern onderzoek concludeerde eerder dit jaar dat de geplande overgang naar het nieuwe systeem niet haalbaar was. Voor erfpachters zijn momenteel nog geen directe gevolgen. Het is niet de eerste keer dat de gemeente recent weer ict-problemen heeft. Begin 2025 liep de invoering van het factuursysteem AFIS in de soep, aldus AT5. items.title: Torrent underground
items.raw_text: When Jane first heard about Memory and Imagination , a rare 1990s documentary about the Library of Congress, she was intrigued. But the Canadian writer in her 30s couldn’t find the movie anywhere — not on streaming services, not on YouTube, not on pirate sites — and her intrigue turned into obsession. Worried it might become a lost film , Jane decided to scour auction sites, search every library catalog she could think of, and even enlist some of her online acquaintances to find a copy. Her plan was to “share it with other people to help ensure it would be preserved into the future,” as she puts it. Jane knew the perfect tool for the task: a private torrent tracker. “I am ethically conflicted about piracy. I often feel guilty about it.” Private trackers are essentially the speakeasies of the online piracy world. Promoted primarily by word of mouth, they rely on secrecy, exclusivity, and strict community rules to shield everything that’s going on behind closed doors from the public’s prying eyes. What unites these communities is that they all use BitTorrent to trade media among like-minded file sharers. But their focuses range widely, from general-purpose trackers with catalogs so broad that they make Netflix look like a niche service to the many specialized communities for categories like Chinese movies, motorsports, visual effects tools, e-learning courses, and Japanese porn. items.title: Nvidia onderzoekt relatie van topman met Chinese Mata Hari
items.raw_text: De raad van bestuur van Nvidia start een onafhankelijk onderzoek naar aanleiding van recente berichtgeving dat oprichter en ceo Jensen Huang het doelwit is geweest van een inlichtingen-operatie vanuit China. De Nvidia-topman had een romantische relatie met een Chinese vrouw die ervan wordt verdacht een spion te zijn voor Chinese inlichtingendiensten. Hoewel de bestuursraad geen reden heeft om aan te nemen dat de nationale veiligheid of bedrijfsgeheimen van Nvidia in het geding zijn gekomen, zal het onderzoek alle beschikbare informatie tegen het licht houden. De Nvidia-topman heeft zijn affaire met deze Chinese Mata Hari volmondig toegegeven. Jensen Huang verontschuldigde zich zondag tegenover zijn medewerkers en zijn gezin. ‘Er is geen excuus voor wat ik deed,’ schrijft hij. Vorig jaar al werd in Amerikaanse regeringskringen bekend dat de Chinese vrouw informatie deelde met de regering in Beijing. Ze gaf toen leiding aan het Singaporese bedrijf Megaspeed International dat samen met Nvidia datacenters in Zuidoost Azië bouwt. In die functie ontwikkelde ze een relatie met Jensen Huang die verder ging dan ‘zakelijk’. Pleitbezorger Opvallend was dat Jensen Huang zich opeens ontpopte als een warm pleitbezorger voor de vrije doorstroom van krachtige ai-chips, precies de componenten waar China om zit te springen. items.title: ‘Ai vormt de grootste bedreiging voor grens­be­vei­li­ging’
items.raw_text: Artificiële intelligentie vormt de grootste bedreiging voor grensbeveiliging. Dat is de belangrijkste conclusie van de top van de Global Identity Trust Association. Identiteit kan dankzij ai beter vervalst worden, terwijl er aan de grens gemiddeld slechts 12 seconden tijd is voor een controle. Meer dan honderd documentexperts van overheden, immigratie- en paspoortautoriteiten en verificatiebedrijven woonden de top van de Global Identity Trust Association (Gita) in Amsterdam bij, die werd georganiseerd door Desko, Keesing Technologies en Foster+Freeman. Volgens de organisatoren van de Gita-conferentie bestaan er 86 soorten reis- en identiteitsdocumenten van 195 landen, met meer dan 250 beveiligingskenmerken en druktechnieken. Ai verhoogt de kans op vervalsingen. Tegelijk wordt ai al volop ingezet bij visum- en paspoortaanvragen. Zo kan technologie grote hoeveelheden visumaanvragen sorteren en patronen herkennen die op fraude wijzen.
